headline: France's Clinical Patience Outlasts Morocco
story: France controlled the quarter-final through midfield superiority and relentless pressing, dominating an encounter that never truly threatened to slip away. Despite equal possession shares, the shape was entirely France's: 22 shots to Morocco's five, five high-press triggers to four, and 8.4 seconds faster average ball recovery. Morocco defended dutifully for an hour, then the dam broke—two goals in six minutes (60', 66') on low expected-goal chances that felt inevitable given France's overwhelming creation.

The numbers explained everything. France's 3.52 expected goals against Morocco's 0.16 was less a match than a masterclass in control: Dembélé (8.6) and Mbappé (8.2) terrorised a backline that had no answer to their movement. Bounou (7.0) worked tirelessly in Morocco's goal, bailing out a defence that weathered 22 shots. France squandered bigger chances—a 0.79-xG save in the 28th minute, a 0.48 miss in the 56th, another 0.65 miss in the 88th—yet the two that counted sufficed to close a quarter-final that was never a contest.

keyMoment.text: France's opening goal—the release that converted dominance into victory

home.verdict: Dominance in chance creation and clinical second-half finishing made Morocco's resistance untenable.
points: 22 shots to Morocco's 5 created unsustainable pressure; one team couldn't handle offensive volume
Dembélé (8.6) and Mbappé (8.2) versus Morocco's best (Diaz 6.8) exposed class gap on wing
Missed 0.79 and 0.65-xG chances; either converted makes Morocco's retreat catastrophically exposed

away.verdict: Starved of possession and creation, they lacked the attacking spark to threaten France.
points: 0.16 xG and 5 shots: offensive plan never threatened, only endured (until it collapsed)
One on-target shot required precise finishing; that single chance defined their attacking output
High press phases (4.1) below France's (5.0); midfield press failed to generate turnovers upfield

statLine: France's 3.52 expected goals to Morocco's 0.16 wasn't merely a quarter-final scoreline—it was an artillery strike against a cavalry charge that never materialised.
